You might wonder what steps to take, when to take them, or if you need to team up with a partner to place a strong bid. The Business Development section is your clear action plan. It guides you seamlessly through every stage of pursuing a contract. Along the way, it also helps you organize the essential agencies and vendors you need to build relationships with, turning a complicated process into a confident strategy. MOVE THROUGH EACH STAGE WITH EASE Federal Opportunity Pipeline When you are ready to pursue a contract, it moves to your Opportunities board. This clear visual layout lets you see exactly where every potential deal stands. You can click any opportunity card to open a detailed view containing your notes, documents, and team collaboration tools. As you complete small actions, simply drag and drop the card through four clear stages: Captured Leads Your top contenders start here. To move forward, simply assign an owner so your team knows exactly who is taking the lead. Qualifications Actively assess if the contract aligns with your business strategy. This ensures you only spend your valuable time on deals you have a high probability of winning. Write and Submit Proposal This is where the focused work happens as you craft a proposal and submit your formal bid. Submitted Status Keep track of your final results so you always know if a bid is pending, won, or lost. If a contract requires teaming up, your opportunity details also include a dedicated partner manager to help you easily coordinate with outside vendors. KNOW THE PLAYERS Accounts Winning government contracts requires knowing exactly who is buying what you sell and who else is operating in your space. The Accounts tool helps you organize these essential relationships. You can easily save profiles directly from your market research to build a clear picture of the landscape. Your accounts are sorted into helpful categories so you always know who is who: Prospects and Customers Track the government agencies you want to work with and the ones you already serve. Partners and Potential Partners Organize the vendors you have successfully teamed up with and those you might want to collaborate with in the future. Competitors Keep an eye on other businesses winning contracts in your field so you can continuously refine your own strategy. BUILD A TRUSTED NETWORK Contacts Government contracting is ultimately about people. Having an incredible product is only half the equation; you also need to connect with the specific individuals who need your solutions and have the authority to buy them. The Contacts tool turns a massive, intimidating government directory into a clear, step by step relationship builder. We help you systematically introduce yourself, track your conversations, and turn cold contacts into trusted, valuable connections. Targeting List Before you start reaching out, you need a strong foundation. This is where you build your ideal list of 200 plus key players. You can easily save contacts directly from your Market Intelligence research or upload your own files. We make it easy to organize a diverse list of program office personnel who need your technology, contracting officers who handle the acquisitions, and small business representatives who can help you navigate the inner workings of an agency. Outreach This is where your targeting list turns into action. Once you know exactly who to contact, this tool helps you get your foot in the door and land that crucial first meeting. You can set up automated introduction emails and scheduled follow ups so you never have to worry about a contact slipping through the cracks if they do not reply right away. It takes the pressure off of daily networking and keeps your outreach moving forward automatically. Relationships Once you have established a genuine connection, that person moves into your permanent network. This is your curated list of trusted contacts and industry allies. These are the people who might point you toward new leads, become future teaming partners, or simply share best practices as you continue to grow your footprint and establish your reputation in the government market. Frequently Asked Questions What is the first step after finding a lead I want to pursue? Once you decide to pursue a lead, it moves directly to your Opportunities board. It keeps your pipeline organized and ensures no deadlines are missed. How do I manage all the different agencies and businesses I need to keep track of? The Accounts section is built specifically for this. It allows you to organize everyone you interact with into clear categories like Prospects, Customers, Partners, and Competitors. You can easily save profiles directly from your market research so your whole team stays completely informed about the players in your space. I have a list of people I want to reach out to. Can GovCon360 help me manage that? Yes. The Contacts tool lets you build a targeted list of government buyers, contracting officers, and potential partners. Finding a great lead is exciting, but knowing exactly what to do next can feel overwhelming. You might wonder what steps to take, when to take them, or if you need to team up with a partner to place a strong bid. The Business Development section is your clear action plan. It guides you seamlessly through every stage of pursuing a contract. Along the way, it also helps you organize the essential agencies and vendors you need to build relationships with, turning a complicated process into a confident strategy.

When you are ready to pursue a contract, it moves to your Opportunities board. This clear visual layout lets you see exactly where every potential deal stands. You can click any opportunity card to open a detailed view containing your notes, documents, and team collaboration tools. As you complete small actions, simply drag and drop the card through four clear stages:
Your top contenders start here. To move forward, simply assign an owner so your team knows exactly who is taking the lead.
Actively assess if the contract aligns with your business strategy. This ensures you only spend your valuable time on deals you have a high probability of winning.
This is where the focused work happens as you craft a proposal and submit your formal bid.
Keep track of your final results so you always know if a bid is pending, won, or lost.
If a contract requires teaming up, your opportunity details also include a dedicated partner manager to help you easily coordinate with outside vendors.

Winning government contracts requires knowing exactly who is buying what you sell and who else is operating in your space. The Accounts tool helps you organize these essential relationships. You can easily save profiles directly from your market research to build a clear picture of the landscape. Your accounts are sorted into helpful categories so you always know who is who:
Track the government agencies you want to work with and the ones you already serve.
Organize the vendors you have successfully teamed up with and those you might want to collaborate with in the future.
Keep an eye on other businesses winning contracts in your field so you can continuously refine your own strategy.

Government contracting is ultimately about people. Having an incredible product is only half the equation; you also need to connect with the specific individuals who need your solutions and have the authority to buy them. The Contacts tool turns a massive, intimidating government directory into a clear, step by step relationship builder. We help you systematically introduce yourself, track your conversations, and turn cold contacts into trusted, valuable connections.

Before you start reaching out, you need a strong foundation. This is where you build your ideal list of 200 plus key players. You can easily save contacts directly from your Market Intelligence research or upload your own files. We make it easy to organize a diverse list of program office personnel who need your technology, contracting officers who handle the acquisitions, and small business representatives who can help you navigate the inner workings of an agency.

This is where your targeting list turns into action. Once you know exactly who to contact, this tool helps you get your foot in the door and land that crucial first meeting. You can set up automated introduction emails and scheduled follow ups so you never have to worry about a contact slipping through the cracks if they do not reply right away. It takes the pressure off of daily networking and keeps your outreach moving forward automatically.

Once you have established a genuine connection, that person moves into your permanent network. This is your curated list of trusted contacts and industry allies. These are the people who might point you toward new leads, become future teaming partners, or simply share best practices as you continue to grow your footprint and establish your reputation in the government market.

Once you decide to pursue a lead, it moves directly to your Opportunities board. Here, you can assign it to a team member and visually track your progress from a newly captured lead all the way to a submitted proposal. It keeps your pipeline organized and ensures no deadlines are missed.

The Accounts section is built specifically for this. It allows you to organize everyone you interact with into clear categories like Prospects, Customers, Partners, and Competitors.
